equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests (17.5% of base pre-NCI equity value)
equity_bridge.note: NCI share of FY2025 adjusted net income 640/(3,022+640) = 17.5%, applied to the base scenario's pre-NCI equity value (EV 90.6bn less economic net debt 43.2bn = 47.3bn -> 8.3bn). Cross-checks: NCI book equity 6,573 + NCI reclassified to liabilities 661 (FY2025 AR, IAS 32) = 7.2bn (1.15x book); 640m NCI earnings at ~13x. Held fixed across scenarios, which slightly overstates the NCI claim in the bear and understates it in the bull.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5y CAGR (31.4%) is meaningless: FY2020 attributable equity of 4.9bn was depressed by the innogy purchase accounting, and revenue 3y (-12%) is the unwind of the FY2022 commodity spike. Reported EPS is distorted by mark-to-market and impairments. Adjusted EBITDA (the regulated-asset-driven line) is the selected growth basis.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF equals reported FCF (SBC-zero, no interest income strip -- E.ON is a net-debt company). FCF CAGRs are undefined: owner FCF is negative in FY2023-FY2025 (-356, -1,298, -937) because cash-effective investments (6.5-8.5bn) exceed OCF during the grid capex supercycle; this is RAB build, not distress (see dcf-methods SKILL: infrastructure in a capex supercycle).

scenario_narratives.base: Grid capex supercycle delivered to plan (EUR48bn 2026-30), 2030 EBITDA ~12.6bn (just under the 13.0bn target), then steady-state growth with the asset base; pre-tax ROCE ~8.3-8.9%, a modest spread over the cost of capital, leaving a thin equity slice after EUR43bn economic net debt and ~17.5% minorities.
scenario_narratives.bull: Fair BNetzA 5th-period returns, sustained connection demand and Ovo synergies: 2030 EBITDA 13.2bn and rising to 16.5bn by 2035, 2.5% terminal growth; the extra capex earns above WACC.
scenario_narratives.bear: Adverse BNetzA 5th-period WACC: same mandated capex at ~7% pre-tax ROCE (no spread over cost of capital), retail squeeze, commissioning delays; 2030 EBITDA ~11.5bn, 1.5% terminal growth, leverage pinned at the 5.0x debt-factor ceiling.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A regulated network is worth roughly its capital base times the spread between allowed return and cost of capital. The component DCF makes that explicit: heavy capex is charged in full as it is spent, D&A and EBITDA follow it with a lag, and the terminal year is forced to steady-state reinvestment so the exit value lands near 1.1x capital employed. Economic net debt (incl. pensions and nuclear AROs) and minorities are deducted once each. The model is very sensitive to the discount rate because the equity is a ~45% slice of enterprise value.
key_risks_to_valuation: WACC: each 0.5pp moves the value by several euros per share because equity is levered ~1:1 against economic net debt
BNetzA 5th regulatory period (power from 2029) allowed equity return -- the single largest driver of 2030s EBITDA
Capex execution and commissioning lag on a EUR48bn programme; leverage near the 5.0x debt-factor ceiling
Legacy nuclear-decommissioning and pension provisions are discount-rate sensitive (in net debt at book)
NCI valued by a profit-share proxy rather than subsidiary-level DCFs
Ovo acquisition consideration and Czech gas sale proceeds not yet in net debt

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 14.98-20.39
data_sources.financials: E.ON Integrated Annual Report 2025 (Economic Net Debt table, Forecast Report, NCI note 23, Adjusted Net Income reconciliation); Q1-2026 results presentation (guidance confirmation, FY2030 targets, 2026-30 capex ~EUR48bn, Q1 END 46.1bn); Capital Markets Story 2025 (RAB EUR46bn, ROCE 8-9%); EOAN.DE_Metrics.csv / kpis for history
data_sources.qualitative: EOAN.DE_Analysis.json (bull/bear case, BNetzA 5th period, Ovo, leverage)

inputs.share_count_basis: ~2,613m ordinary shares outstanding (FY2025 AR; FY2026 EPS guidance 'based on around 2,613 million shares'). No dilutive equity awards: E.ON's LTI is a cash-settled virtual-share plan. Held flat -- no buyback programme and no equity raise planned (capex funded by debt within the <=5.0x debt-factor ceiling).
inputs.net_debt_basis: E.ON's own Economic Net Debt at 2025-12-31: financial liabilities 37,295 (innogy bonds at nominal, incl. lease liabilities) + FX hedging adj 110 + provisions for pensions 4,408 + asset-retirement obligations 6,361 (largely PreussenElektra nuclear decommissioning) = total_debt 48,174; less liquid funds 4,352 and non-current securities 586 = cash 4,938. Pensions and AROs are debt-like and are charged here ONCE; their cash utilisation is therefore not deducted again from the flows (adjusted EBITDA excludes it). Q1-2026 END was 46,140 (2026-03-31) but that is the seasonal Q1 trough (Q1 FCF -2.4bn, margining) and already contains part of FY2026's capex, which the model charges in full in year 1; pairing the 31-Dec-2025 balance sheet with FY2026 full-year flows avoids charging Q1 2026 capex twice. H1-2026 (Aug-2026) report is not in the extracted set and should be added at the next refresh.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero for valuation purposes: E.ON's Performance Matching Plan/LTI is a cash-settled virtual-share scheme (FY2025 AR 'Share-Based Payment' note), expensed in personnel costs inside adjusted EBITDA; no equity-settled awards and no net-share-settlement taxes (EquityAwardTaxes 0 every year). CSV StockBasedComp of ~EUR11m is the cash-settled charge already in EBITDA, so it is not deducted again.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR-built: risk-free 2.7% (10y Bund), ERP 5.5%, levered beta 0.90 (asset beta ~0.5 for regulated networks relevered at E.ON's ~47% market-value leverage) -> cost of equity ~7.65%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~3.9% (recent EUR benchmark issues), 25% tax -> 2.9%. Weights: market cap ~48.5bn vs economic net debt 43.2bn -> E 53% / D 47% -> 5.4%, rounded to 5.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged in the scenario flows (BNetzA 5th-period return, capex execution), not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities (~EUR3.1bn) sit inside E.ON's financial liabilities and therefore inside net_debt; lease principal (financing cash flow) is NOT deducted from the flows, and right-of-use renewal is covered by the capex line. Adjusted EBITDA is post-IFRS-16.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; NCI is deducted ONCE in the equity bridge (see equity_bridge). NCI share of FY2025 adjusted operating earnings was EUR640m against EUR3,022m attributable adjusted net income -> 17.5% of group adjusted net income. NCI is mostly municipal co-owners of German regional DSOs (Westenergie/Avacon/E.DIS/Bayernwerk-type holdings) and CEE network subsidiaries. Valued at 17.5% of base-case pre-NCI equity value (see bridge note).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF component route with the non-US adaptations (routing table: 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'). The skill has no separate regulated-utility/RAB row; a RAB-multiple model was considered but the component DCF is equivalent when driven by explicit capex and D&A paths: capital employed (~EUR70bn, ROCE 8.9% pre-tax FY2025) grows by capex minus D&A, and the terminal year is set to steady state (net investment ~2% of capital employed = terminal growth), so the terminal value lands near 1.1x terminal capital employed -- the regulated-asset sanity check is built in. Revenue is ~75% commodity pass-through (Energy Retail, network fees), so the same revenue path is used in all scenarios and the scenarios differ in EUR EBITDA, D&A and capex expressed as % of that revenue. FY0 anchors: FY2025 revenue 78,704; adjusted EBITDA 9,849 reported / 9,419 restated ex value-neutral regulatory timing effects (the FY2026 guidance basis); adjusted D&A ~3.6bn; cash-effective investments 8,509; OCF 7,003; reported FCF (OCF - investments) -937. Year-1 EBITDA 9.5bn = mid of FY2026 guidance 9.4-9.6bn; year-1 capex 8.7bn = FY2026 guidance; 2026-2030 capex sums to ~EUR48bn (company plan); base 2030 EBITDA 12.6bn vs company target ~13.0bn. Structural breaks NOT used as a base: FY2016 Uniper spin, FY2017 EUR10bn nuclear-fund payment (OCF -2,952), FY2019-20 innogy consolidation, FY2022 price-spike revenue (115.7bn). Excluded from net debt: pending Ovo (UK retail) acquisition, price undisclosed; Czech gas-distribution sale proceeds (closing H1-2026). Both are small against EUR43bn of net debt and should be added once the H1/9M-2026 balance sheet is extracted. Buybacks: none (non-repurchaser; flat count needs no funding because there is no SBC dilution).

bear.ebitda_margin_path_note: EUR EBITDA 9.4 / 9.8 / 10.3 / 10.8 / 11.5 (2030, ~12% below the 13.0bn target) then 12.0 / 12.4 / 12.8 / 13.2 / 13.6bn; terminal pre-tax ROCE ~7.0% on ~111bn capital employed (vs 8.9% FY2025).
bear.capex_pct_path_note: EUR capex 8.7 / 9.3 / 9.6 / 9.8 / 9.9 (~47bn: the obligation to connect does not shrink with the return) then 9.0 / 8.5 / 8.1 / 7.8 / 7.6bn.
bear.narrative: BNetzA sets a 5th-period equity return (power from 2029) below what E.ON's CFO calls fair financing cost, so roughly the same mandated capex earns a pre-tax ROCE nearer 7% (post-tax ~5.3%, at or just below WACC, so new investment creates no value); retail margins compress under UK/German competition and Ovo integration costs; connection backlogs and supply chains delay commissioning so EBITDA lags spend. Leverage drifts to the 5.0x debt-factor ceiling, forcing either a slower programme or a dividend reset, and legacy nuclear/mining provisions re-rate with discount rates. Terminal growth 1.5% (inflation-only RAB indexation).

base.growth_rates_note: Revenue is a denominator: FY2026 -8% (Q1-2026 sales -13% YoY on lower retail commodity prices, NEW Group deconsolidation, Romania sale, German transmission-fee subsidy), then ~2-2.5% (network fee growth with RAB, retail flat).
base.ebitda_margin_path_note: EUR adjusted EBITDA 9.5 / 10.2 / 10.9 / 11.7 / 12.6 (2030; company target ~13.0, haircut ~3% for BNetzA 5th period from 2029) then 13.2 / 13.7 / 14.2 / 14.7 / 15.2bn. Terminal pre-tax ROCE ~8.3% on ~EUR111bn capital employed vs 8.9% FY2025.
base.da_pct_path_note: EUR D&A 3.8 rising to 6.0bn as the 48bn programme is commissioned (~18-19 yr average life on capital employed, matching FY2025's 3.6bn on ~70bn).
base.capex_pct_path_note: EUR cash-effective investments 8.7 (FY2026 guidance) / 9.4 / 9.8 / 10.0 / 10.1 (sum ~48bn = 2026-2030 plan), then tapering 9.5 / 9.1 / 8.7 / 8.4 / 8.2bn. Terminal capex 8.2 = D&A 6.0 + net investment 2.2 (= 2% terminal growth x ~111bn capital employed) -- steady state, not a perpetual supercycle.
base.cash_tax_rate_path_note: Unlevered tax on EBIT. FY2025 cash taxes 828m vs adj. EBT ~4.9bn (~17%) plus the interest shield implies ~19% on EBIT; accelerated tax depreciation during the capex ramp keeps cash tax below the 25% sustainable operating rate, ramping to 25% by year 10.
base.wc_capture_pct_note: Working capital is dominated by margining and regulatory timing balances that E.ON itself reports as value-neutral; no structural capture modelled.
base.terminal_cap_multiple_note: Cap set above the base Gordon multiple (1.02/0.035 = 29x terminal FCF) so Gordon governs the base: terminal FCF is a steady-state regulated stream after net investment, and 29x FCF corresponds to ~8x terminal EBITDA / ~1.1x terminal capital employed -- a sub-market multiple for a regulated network. The cap binds in the bull case (2.5% growth -> 34x).
base.narrative: German grid capex supercycle delivered roughly to plan: EUR48bn invested 2026-2030, Energy Networks RAB compounding ~8-9%/yr, group EBITDA reaching ~12.6bn in 2030 (3% short of the 13.0bn target as the BNetzA 5th regulatory period trims the allowed equity return modestly), retail flat at ~1.7bn. After 2030 investment tapers toward a steady state and EBITDA grows with the asset base. The business earns a pre-tax ROCE of ~8.3-8.9%, only modestly above its after-tax cost of capital, so value is close to capital employed plus a small spread -- and the equity is the thin slice left after EUR43bn of economic net debt and ~17.5% minorities.

bull.capex_pct_path_note: EUR capex 8.7 / 9.6 / 10.2 / 10.5 / 10.8 (~49.8bn, upper end incl. Sondervermoegen-driven connection demand) then 10.4 / 10.0 / 9.6 / 9.3 / 9.0bn; terminal net investment 2.65bn ~ 2.5% growth on a larger base.
bull.narrative: BNetzA's 5th-period framework lands at a return that fairly compensates grid investment (CFO's lobbying succeeds, or courts force it), grid-connection demand (data centres, heat pumps, batteries, Sondervermoegen infrastructure money) keeps the 2030s investment rate high, E.ON beats its ~13.0bn 2030 EBITDA target, Ovo scales UK retail at good synergies, and the RAB keeps compounding at ~2.5% real-plus-inflation into perpetuity. Higher capex here is value-creating because it earns above WACC.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 30x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% house default because the dominant driver is a single regulator (BNetzA's unresolved 5th-period return for ~60% of EBITDA) and management itself has publicly criticised the draft. Bull cut to 25% because it needs both a favourable regulatory outcome and above-plan execution of a record capex programme. Base at 50% reflects E.ON's record of meeting guidance (FY2025 at the upper end).
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
